simple.meaning: צְרִיחַ (tsᵉrîyach) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a citadel.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 9:46. The surrounding context includes death, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צְרִיחַ (H6877) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: צְרִיחַ (tsᵉrîyach) / H6877 is traced through Judges 9:46, Judges 9:49, 1 Samuel 13:6 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: When all the men of the tower of Shechem heard of it, they entered into the stronghold of the house of Elberith.

timeline.evidenceText: When all the men of the tower of Shechem heard of it, they entered into the stronghold of the house of Elberith.

All the people likewise each cut down his bough, followed Abimelech, and put them at the base of the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire over them, so that all the people of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women.

definitions.full: H6877. tseriach צְרִיחַ noun [masculine] perhaps excavation, underground chamber ; — ׳צ absolute Judg 9:49 , construct 9:46 ; plural צְרִחִים 1Sam 13:6 ; — used as hiding-places 13:6 (+ בֹּרוֺת סְלָעִים, חֲוָחִים, מְעָרוֺת, ); as refuge Judg 9:46 (where connected with shrine), 9:49 (Vrss stronghold ; on uncertainty of meaning see GFM). צֹרִי see I. צֹר . צְרֻיָה צְרִי, צֳרִי, see צרה . above, צרך (√ of following; Late Hebrew צָרַךְ have need of ; Arabic be needy , so Aramaic צְרַךְ , ( צ , = !); Christian-Palestinian Aramaic χρεία ).
